annotation.title_clean: Part 124—Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System Authority for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Law Enforcement and Correctional Agencies
annotation.title_en: Part 124—Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System Authority for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Law Enforcement and Correctional Agencies
annotation.authors_or_issuer: U.S. Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Department of Justice
annotation.venue: Federal Register (6 CFR part 124 / 28 CFR part 124)
annotation.summary_en: Joint DHS/DOJ regulation implementing the SAFER SKIES Act, governing how state, local, tribal and territorial law enforcement and correctional agencies may detect, warn, and mitigate threatening drones. It sets FBI-run NCUTC certification, agency policies, authorized technology lists, FAA/FCC coordination, reporting, privacy limits, audits and penalties.
key_provisions_or_claims: Mitigation requires NCUTC Mitigation Certification and a Part 107 remote pilot certificate; only agency employees, not contractors, may mitigate.
Mitigation needs a credible threat determination and must be proportionate, using the least disruptive effective means.
Agencies must file advance notification (30 days), a signed C-UAS Operations Plan, real-time ATC notice, and 48-hour post-operation reports.
Only technologies on the Authorized Technologies and Systems Lists may be deployed; control communications are retained at most 180 days.
Violations of Federal coordination requirements risk fines up to $100,000 per violation or suspension; authority terminates December 31, 2031.
